parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-26, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 17.9 | 13.68 | 13.68
2 | 50.4 | 5.82 | 19.50
3 | 514.6 | 0.68 | 20.18
4 | 502.0 | 17.67 | 37.85
5 | 194.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AKQ-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-26, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station T-26 (Survey Area T)**

Station T-26 features a 5-layer geoelectric succession:
- **Layer 1:** 17.9 Ω·m, thickness 13.68 m (depth: 0–13.68 m) – low-resistivity top layer.
- **Layer 2:** 50.4 Ω·m, thickness 5.82 m (depth: 13.68–19.50 m) – weathered zone.
- **Layer 3:** 514.6 Ω·m, thickness 0.68 m (depth: 19.50–20.18 m) – highly resistive thin band.
- **Layer 4:** 502.0 Ω·m, thickness 17.67 m (depth: 20.18–37.85 m) – resistive unit.
- **Layer 5:** 194.4 Ω·m, substratum extending from 37.85 m depth.

Evaluating consecutive triplets gives:
- Layers 1–2–3 ($r_1 < r_2 < r_3$): **A**
- Layers 2–3–4 ($r_2 < r_3 > r_4$): **K**
- Layers 3–4–5 ($r_3 > r_4 > r_5$): **Q**

The resulting curve is **AKQ**, confirming that the classification on file is correct.

{"curve_type_stated": "AKQ", "label_issue_flagged": false}
